title: Beyond Gimmicks: Turning Jung's Theory into Marketing Tools
text: Hello, this is Liam in for Komal. Brands keep asking for personality. Jung gave the theory, 12 archetypes gave the map, and AI is starting to turn that map into a daily marketing tool. Watch how. Here is the whole idea in one breath. Jungian archetypes are recurring character patterns humans already understand. Marketers use them so a brand feels like one person, not a committee. An AI tool can make that personality show up in every headline, email, and campaign, not just a workshop slide. Carl Jung called them archetypes, characters living in what he named the collective unconscious, not invented by one ad agency, shared. The hero, the sage, the caregiver, you recognize them before anyone defines them.

title: The Mark & Pearson Wheel: 12 Business Archetypes Explained
text: Branding borrowed the wheel. Mark and Pearson mapped 12 archetypes for business: innocent, sage, explorer, hero, outlaw, magician, everyman, lover, jester, caregiver, creator, ruler. Pick a primary, name a shadow. Every downstream choice, copy tone, visual palette, feature emphasis follows from that character. Why marketers care? An archetype is a shortcut to consistency. Tone of voice, a sage does not joke like a jester. Positioning, a hero challenges, a caregiver protects. Every touchpoint reads as the same character, ads, website, support, social, because the archetype is the operating system underneath. Without a tool, archetypes die in a workshop deck.
